response.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_avg_ratio, AVG(line_item_count) AS avg_line_items_per_order_item FROM (SELECT order_item_id, AVG(derived_product_cost * 1.0 / NULLIF(derived_total_cost, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS line_item_count FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY order_item_id) AS per_item;

assumptions.assumption: Only order items that have at least one invoice line item are counted, so order items with no invoice line items are excluded from both averages.

A ratio is missing when either derived_product_cost or derived_total_cost is NULL, or when derived_total_cost is 0. Zero totals are turned into NULL with NULLIF to avoid division by zero, and the average skips them.

The number of invoice line items for an order item counts all its rows, including rows whose ratio is missing. An order item whose ratios are all missing has a NULL average. It is ignored in the overall ratio average but still counted in the line-item average.

alternatives.interpretation: Include every order item from Order_Items, so those with no invoice line items count as 0 line items. Their ratio is NULL and is ignored in the ratio average.
alternatives.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_avg_ratio, AVG(line_item_count) AS avg_line_items_per_order_item FROM (SELECT oi.order_item_id, AVG(ili.derived_product_cost * 1.0 / NULLIF(ili.derived_total_cost, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(ili.order_item_id) AS line_item_count FROM Order_Items oi LEFT JOIN Invoice_Line_Items ili ON ili.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id GROUP BY oi.order_item_id) AS per_item;
